newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends 5.6 pct higher after budget day.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends 5.6 pct higher after budget day.

text.p: A spate of buy orders on the back of a bullish market undertone boosted blue chips at Bombay bourses on Saturday, after Friday's 97/98 budget was widely perceived as a tonic for a bull run, dealers said.
Prices zoomed to dizzy heights in a day of euphoric trade.
"The mood is very buoyant. The Finance Minister has done an excellent job in taking the (liberalisation) baton forward," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive at Lloyds Securities.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced sharp cuts in corporate and income taxes, allowed firms to buy back shares and upped limits on foreign institutional investment in some firms.

The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange capped a sizzling five percent Friday rally by notching a net gain of 5.56 percent on Saturday. The index ended at a provisional 3,854.90 compared to Friday's close of 3,651.91.
"This is a sustained bull run that has been started. The major factor is the substantial reduction in tax rates," said dealer Govind Agarwal at local brokerage Motilal Oswal.
"One can't even dream of such a budget. Mr Chidambaram has set the entire economy in an era. It is truly revolutionary."
Tax on domestic firms was reduced to 35 percent from 40 percent, and on foreign firms to 48 percent from 55 percent.

Before the budget, analysts were cautiously optimistic about market reforms that were needed to be carried out by a fractious 15-party centre-left goverment, which had to kickstart a slowing economy and rebuild confidence among the domestic investors.

"Happy days are here again. The budget brings back the prodigal Indian investor to contribute to the process of vital capital formation," said A.K.T. Janak, president, investment banking division at Apple Finance Ltd.
Among Friday's top market gainers were Gujarat Ambuja Cement, Castrol, Colgate, Bajaj Auto, IDBI and State Bank of India.
